title: Python version guidance conflicts with the only declared target
reasoning: The repository configuration targets Python 3.11 for Ruff, but the setup instructions tell developers to download the latest Python and create a venv with whatever python is on PATH. With no visible requires-python metadata or documented supported version, new environments may use a newer interpreter than the project is validated against, which can break native or compiled dependencies and produce behavior that differs from CI or production.
recommendation: Document the supported Python version explicitly and add project metadata or an environment file that enforces it, such as requires-python in pyproject.toml plus README setup commands using Python 3.11.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are listed for this metadata feature, and interpreter-version drift is a setup-time problem rather than an application behavior covered by unit tests.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI matrix or setup check that fails when the project is installed on unsupported Python versions.
minimumFixScope: Clarify README prerequisites and add an enforceable Python version declaration in project metadata or tooling configuration.
